title: Not by bread alone (Deuteronomy 8:1–3)
hook: the hunger in the wilderness taught them to live by every word

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Shema: hear, and love with all your heart, soul and might. Your line was on your doorposts. Did a doorway remind you of anything? Day four hundred seven.

It's about four in the afternoon and you skipped lunch. You know the feeling. A low hum in your stomach, then a tightness, then you're short with someone who didn't deserve it. Hunger is honest. It shows you, very fast, how much you depend on things you usually don't think about. Now picture forty years of depending, every single morning, on food that falls with the dew and rots if you save it. Moses is near the end of his life, and in Deuteronomy he's looking back at those years with the people. And he says something surprising about the hunger. It wasn't an accident. It was a lesson.
screen: `FOUR O'CLOCK, NO LUNCH.` → `HUNGER IS HONEST.` → `THE HUNGER WAS A LESSON.`

segments.voice: Moses says, in the King James Bible: "thou shalt remember all the way which the LORD thy God led thee these forty years in the wilderness." Remember the whole road. And then: "he humbled thee, and suffered thee to hunger, and fed thee with manna, which thou knewest not, neither did thy fathers know; that he might make thee know that man doth not live by bread only, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of the LORD doth man live." Look at the order. First the hunger. Then the manna, a food nobody had ever seen, so nobody could take credit for it. And then the lesson: you need bread, yes, and you also need something bread can't give. You need the word that comes from God. Moses adds a tender detail a few verses later: in all those forty years, your clothes didn't wear out, and your feet didn't swell. Carried, even when it didn't feel like it. Many centuries later, in the Gospels, Jesus is alone in the wilderness for forty days, fasting, and he's hungry. The tempter says: if you're the Son of God, turn these stones into bread. And Jesus answers with this exact verse from Deuteronomy. In the King James Bible's version of Matthew: "Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God." It's why many Christians fast, during Lent or before communion or at other times: not to punish the body, but to let a little hunger remind them what else they live on.
screen: `REMEMBER ALL THE WAY.` · `FIRST THE HUNGER, THEN THE MANNA.` · `CLOTHES THAT DIDN'T WEAR OUT.` · `JESUS ANSWERS WITH THIS VERSE.` · then, large: `MAN SHALL NOT LIVE BY BREAD ALONE.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: go hungry a little, and listen. Only if it's safe for you: if you're pregnant, unwell, or have any history with food that makes this hard, skip the hunger and just do the listening. Otherwise, choose a small fast today: one snack, one coffee, one dessert you let go by. For now, settle and breathe, and notice what you're hungry for beyond food. Rest. Attention. Being known. A word from God. When the hunger comes later, let it be a bell that reminds you. If you pray, you can turn each pang into a short prayer. The bell holds the time.
Not by bread alone. Moses' lesson from forty years of manna, and the verse Jesus answered with in the wilderness.
Your line: not by bread alone. Today, skip one small thing you'd normally eat or drink, and when you miss it, ask what else you're hungry for. Day four hundred seven.

howItsDone: Many Christians fast at certain times, such as Lent, Fridays or before communion, and Orthodox and Catholic Christians keep set fasting days; the verse is often quoted to explain why.

trapdoor: what you thought: a saying about not being materialistic.
what it means: the hunger in the desert taught a people that they live by bread and also by God's word.
what a scholar hears: Deuteronomy 8:3, quoted by Jesus in Matthew 4:4 and Luke 4:4; all three of his answers to the tempter come from Deuteronomy.
